category_title: Multilingual learners who view dialogue as a tool for peer support and collaborative meaning-making
student_description: Nico is an enthusiastic but insecure reader who struggles with his reading identity due to leveled assessment systems. When recalling complex plot details, he tends to fragment his storytelling and use elongated pauses. He uniquely requires convergent questioning to anchor his thoughts in the moment, and collaborative peer discussion to catalyze his writing over time.

criteria.rationale: Nico views dialogue as a tool for peer support and relies on verbalizing his ideas with others to successfully transition into independent writing.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate regular, structured opportunities for peer collaboration or turn-and-talk discussions immediately prior to writing tasks.

criteria.rationale: Because Nico struggles with his identity as a reader due to leveled systems, he needs an inviting environment with high-interest materials to foster a positive, independent association with reading.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include provisions for an inviting physical space or dedicated access to high-interest, choice-based reading materials (e.g., books about his specific interests like dinosaurs).
